## Notes

### Quick read
- Ali is a blonde, high-output yapper mom of three (toddler boy plus a nursing newborn) filming in her own home, and she already has 7 ads running with the best ROAS profile in the V3 batch.
- Best next move: send the ideas Fatima promised on Sep 22 (still owed), steering her toward the nursing angle that got "Really good one! love this" and away from doll demos.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- Who she is on camera: mom of three, blonde, bright pink nails, pink skirt or shorts almost every video, "Amazing Grace" daisy tee in the recent batch. Films at home (kitchen/entry with a laundry area and front door visible, Gabe's shopping bag, toys on the floor). Real kids: a blond toddler boy (black tee, jeans, boots) and, in the Sep 22 video, a newborn she nurses in the sling. Several demos use a baby doll instead of a real baby (Sep 12 and Sep 17 "POV clingy baby" and "You've got it all wrong" sets).
- Format: mostly yapper talking straight to camera, calm to mid energy, confident sales voice, ends every script with a sale/scarcity CTA ("huge sale", "cute patterns sell out"). Two sub-formats: (1) 22s silent-ish routine clip (doing chores, toddler tugs, puts sling on, carries him plus a box) with a text hook and voiceover; (2) 39 to 42s talking head that holds up her pile of old bulky carriers, shows the padded strap close up, and walks through putting it on. Also a quick 11 to 13s text-only POV demo.
- Hooks she uses: "Give me literally 30 seconds", "For the stage 5 clingers", "Why didn't they tell me?", "I understand now...", "your toddler wants held when you have 47 things to do", "'Hold me' survival tool", "Bulky carriers are out", "Stop buying carriers you'll only use twice", "POV: you have a clingy baby AND things to do", "Nursing moms,", "You've got it all wrong!", "In case you didn't know...". She makes many hook variants of one body, which is exactly the volume habit Fatima wants.
- What worked: all six Sep 2 routine videos were approved and ran as ads (0862e55e, 13697d7f, 5ef2c3c9, 5a0404e4, 0f653fed, plus 0f9feea7 from Sep 17), and 9e66828a ("Hold me survival tool" talking head) also ran. $109 earnings, $912 Trybe GMV, ROAS 1.3 on $1,044 spend since June. Sep 22 nursing video approved with "Really good one! love this".
- What got rejected: two Sep 12 clips for a visible CapCut watermark (047d4fa9, bad21e6e); three for saying "hands free" (a018fbbd, e16d0299, f2551b6e). She fixed it and resubmitted the carrier talking head without "hands free" (approved Sep 17). Two Sep 12 duplicates (d4a7f5aa, 313759a6) are still pending; 313759a6 still says "hands-free all day" in the transcript, so it should be rejected, and d4a7f5aa ("You've got it all wrong") also says "Totally hands-free".
- Safety and checklist issues seen:
  - a018fbbd (rejected): both hands up waving with toddler in sling under "Totally hands-free", then toddler lying sideways across her; on-screen text says "Holds babies 12-45 lb" (wrong, approved range is 10 to 50 lbs).
  - 047d4fa9 (rejected): both hands up waving with doll in sling at the end.
  - 0f653fed (approved, running as ad): at about 20s she holds a frozen food box with both hands and no hand is visible on the toddler. Worth a look before scaling that ad.
  - Doll use in the correction and POV videos: reads as fake up close and hides the real fit; real toddler videos are stronger.
  - Nursing video: newborn feeding sideways in the sling with her hand on baby, legs dangling out the bottom; fine for a nursing moment, but the seat under bottom and M position are not really shown.
- Strengths to lean on: volume and hook variety, clean scripts that already use the "strain off your arms and back" angle, real messy-home authenticity, a real toddler who actually goes in the sling.
- To improve: always a real baby, not a doll; one hand visibly on baby in every frame, especially when carrying groceries; export without the CapCut end card.
